producer_report.summary: I rewrote the contract, the five role frames and the four capability prompts to hold only each role's job, hard rules, severity definitions and every phrase a test or check reads. Explanation and examples moved to a new optional file, docs/agent-reference.md. Each of the five frames (reader, planner, critic, producer, verifier) gets one line: "Optional: if docs/agent-reference.md exists in the working copy, read it for …; every rule is stated here." The doc exists only in Athena's own repository and is not compiled in, so on other repositories the pointer finds nothing and the frames stand alone. Sizes in estimated tokens (bytes/3, rounded up), before then after: contract 326→310, reader 1997→1895, producer 1257→1018, verifier 1298→1153, planner 1217→1079, critic 974→955. `BudgetSet::Producer` drops from 1300 to 1200, so the planner (the largest set measured against it) uses 89.9%. `BudgetSet::Verifier` stays at 1300 because its largest set (study verifier, 1153) is already under 90%; no budget rises. Contract and Reader budgets are unchanged, so their headroom grows to 40 and 105 tokens; the CHANGELOG says so. In `lib.rs` I also added the test `frames_name_the_reference_doc_as_optional_and_it_exists` and made two ratchets: the contract size test is now `<= 977` and the frame bound is 800. Because a test forces it, the six budget lines in docs/system-facts.md (digits only) are updated. The full `cargo test --locked` passed (exit 0).

open_issues: User question, unanswered: docs/agent-reference.md exists only in Athena's own repository and is read at run time, not compiled in. On other repositories the pointer finds nothing. Do you accept that, or do you want it compiled into the binary (which needs edits to xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS, the ci.yml cache keys and the nine-glob assertion in xtask/tests/policy.rs)?

User question, unanswered: Contract (350) and Reader (2000) were not lowered, because run_pin_tests.rs and live.rs pin those literals. Do you want them lowered too, with those two files added as deliverables?
Verifier stays at 1300 (planner and Producer moved to 1200). Reaching 1250 would need roughly 25 more tokens cut from the study verifier set, which the plan limits to wording trims.
docs/system-facts.md is not a listed deliverable. I edited its six budget lines because tests fail otherwise.
mistakes: In the first reader rewrite I cut 'unless the request says otherwise'. A pinned briefs.rs test caught it and I restored the phrase.

My first prompt pass made the critic set larger and the verifier set barely smaller, because the added pointer line cost more than the cuts saved. I cut deeper and shortened the pointer to 'Optional: …'.
The first CHANGELOG draft used a table and blank lines inside the bullet. Readers of the file find items by content, so I rewrote it as plain indented lines.
learnings: The reader frame is pinned by a briefs.rs test: the phrases 'record each applicable one as an acceptance criterion' and 'do not ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise' must stay. Beyond the plan's anchor list, other tests read frame wording, so run `cargo test -p athena-context` after each prompt edit.
The critic frame could not shrink: its lines are nearly all pinned or severity rules. It dropped only 19 tokens at the set level, mostly from the shorter contract.
Both docs/system-facts.md budget tests (match computed, drift rejected) fail on any prompt byte change, so the facts lines must be updated after every edit.
The largest producer-class set is the planner, not a capability producer, and the largest verifier-class set is the study verifier. The planner and the study verifier set the 90% targets.
The CHANGELOG is read by content, so the new bullet is plain indented lines with no table and no blank lines inside it.
desires: An allowed way to read a background job's output file, which sat outside the working directory. I could only wait for the completion notice, and a second cargo run hit the busy build slot and failed with 'no build slot free for 300 s'.
A tool that reports file byte sizes, to size prompts without `ls -l`.
